security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, literal searches, and legitimate local signing examples. Unquoted shell placeholders create an injection risk, and the credential-testing workflow requires stronger authorization controls despite the ethics notice.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use unquoted placeholders for user-provided paths and tags.
remediation.suggestion: Quote every substituted value, validate paths, add option terminators where supported, and prefer argument-array execution instead of shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The workflow recommends testing discovered credentials against IoT devices without an explicit authorization gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmed ownership, written scope, and user approval before authentication attempts. Default to reporting credentials without testing them.

content.value_statement: Android APK internals are difficult to inspect in packaged form. This skill guides decoding, resource review, smali analysis, rebuilding, signing, and troubleshooting with Apktool.
actual_capabilities: Provides full, code-only, and resource-only APK decoding workflows.
Explains Apktool output, including manifests, resources, smali, assets, and native libraries.
Guides manifest review for permissions, exported components, backup settings, debugging, and network configuration.
Shows local searches for URLs, hardcoded credentials, cryptography, file operations, and native library usage.
Guides APK rebuilding, signing, signature verification, and zip alignment.
Covers framework management, report generation, and common decode or build failures.
limitations: Requires Apktool, Java, and any referenced command-line utilities to be installed.
Produces smali rather than readable Java source; complex review may require Jadx.
Obfuscation, encryption, or missing vendor frameworks can reduce analysis quality.
Commands create files and can overwrite directories or change Apktool framework state.

use_cases.title: Review a mobile application
use_cases.description: Decode an authorized APK and inspect its manifest, resources, and smali for security weaknesses.

use_cases.title: Diagnose an Android build
use_cases.description: Inspect packaged resources, rebuild approved changes, sign the test APK, and troubleshoot failures.

use_cases.title: Map IoT companion behavior
use_cases.description: Locate device endpoints, certificate pinning, native libraries, and communication classes without contacting devices.

prompt_templates.title: Decode an APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Decode [APK path] into [output directory], preserve the original, and summarize the generated directory structure.

prompt_templates.title: Review manifest and resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [decoded directory]. Report permissions, exported components, backup and debug settings, network configuration, URLs, and suspected hardcoded secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Trace IoT communication
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [decoded directory] for IoT endpoints, certificate pinning, native libraries, and related smali classes. Do not contact any endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild an authorized test APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Rebuild [decoded directory] as [output APK], validate changed smali and XML, sign with a test key, verify, and report each artifact.

output_examples.input: Inspect the decoded manifest for security-relevant configuration.
output: Manifest review: package and SDK levels identified.
Permissions: sensitive permissions grouped by purpose.
Components: exported activities, services, and receivers listed.
Configuration: backup, debugging, cleartext traffic, and network security settings summarized.

output_examples.input: Search an IoT companion APK for device communication details.
output: Endpoints: candidate service URLs and device addresses listed with source locations.
Transport: certificate pinning and trust-management references summarized.
Code map: relevant smali classes and native libraries identified.
Safety: no endpoint contacted and no credential tested.

output_examples.input: Rebuild and verify an authorized modified APK.
output_examples.output: The APK was rebuilt, aligned, signed with a test key, and verified. The report lists artifact paths and any build warnings.

best_practices: Analyze only APKs you own or have permission to test, and preserve an untouched copy.
Quote and validate every path before running commands, especially when force overwrite is enabled.
Use protected test keys, verify signatures, and keep debug-signed APKs out of production.
anti_patterns: Do not substitute untrusted text directly into shell commands or use force overwrite without checking the destination.
Do not contact endpoints or test extracted credentials without confirmed authorization and scope.
Do not distribute modified APKs or sign production releases with debug keys.

faq.question: Does this skill install Apktool or Java?
faq.answer: No. Install Apktool, a compatible Java runtime, and any referenced utilities before using the workflows.

faq.question: Can it produce readable Java source?
faq.answer: Apktool produces smali bytecode. Use Jadx alongside it when readable Java output is needed.

faq.question: Can it rebuild modified APKs?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides rebuilding, alignment, signing, and verification for APKs you are authorized to modify.

faq.question: Does APK analysis require network access?
faq.answer: No network access is required for decoding. Endpoint or credential testing requires separate tools, explicit authorization, and user approval.

faq.question: How are possible secrets handled?
faq.answer: Searches run against local decoded files. Protect reports and extracted resources because they may contain sensitive application data.

faq.question: Will it work with obfuscated or system APKs?
faq.answer: It can decode them, but names may remain unreadable. System APKs may also require matching vendor framework resources.
